messages:
ricardo: Customer on prod (acct 112233) reports refunds not applied — instead a credit was applied. Repro below, can someone triage?

ricardo: Repro curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{
    \"model\":\"redwood-alpha-1\",
    \"input\":\"Refund $42 for txn_9876 - customer requested a refund to original payment method\",
    \"tools\":[\"issue_refund\",\"apply_credit\"]
  }'
```

ricardo: Response we saw from routing: 
```
{\"tool\": \"apply_credit\", \"args\": {\"invoice_id\": \"inv_9876\", \"amount\": 42.00}}
```

ricardo: Then billing shows a store credit (balance +42) instead of refund to txn_9876. When we tried to call issue_refund directly we hit a schema error: 
```
refund_service: validation error: missing required field 'transaction_id'
400 Bad Request
```

support-bot: Automated ticket created: INC-4321. Attaching request_id if present will speed debugging. :robot_face:

maya: @ricardo can you paste the request_id and full headers? also which region?

ricardo: request_id=rx_2026_0007_us-east_1_5f3a, region=us-east-1. headers: user-agent=internal-agent/2.1, x-client-app=checkout-service

priya: Quick guess: tool_choice misrouted to apply_credit because the model saw invoice-like tokens in the text. Both tools expose similar surface names and overlapping descriptions.

ash: FYI root cause appears to be ambiguity in function signatures:
- issue_refund(params: {transaction_id: string, amount: number, reason?: string})
- apply_credit(params: {invoice_id: string, amount: number, note?: string})

ash: The model picked apply_credit and then we translated intent into invoice_id which the refund path doesn't accept. So the refund path failed later when customer attempted manual retry.

maya: Can we reproduce locally with the same model + tool catalog? I can try to seed the same prompt.

ricardo: Yes repro is deterministic for this prompt on redwood-alpha-1 with current tool metadata. I ran it 3x, same selection.

priya: Temporary mitigation suggestion: gateway validation that compares chosen_tool args to expected schema and rejects or flags mismatches before executing. That would prevent silent wrong-side effects.

jamie: For a faster short-term fix: add a routing override — if input contains 'txn_' or 'transaction' prefer issue_refund. We can implement as a pattern rule in call-router.

ash: Long-term fix: make function signatures less ambiguous. Options: require an explicit 'target_type' enum (\"transaction\" vs \"invoice\") in both tools, or unify into a single 'refund' tool with explicit mode. Also update tool descriptions to reduce lexical overlap.

ops-bot: Deploy note: canary rule push to call-router in us-east-1 scheduled now (rollback in 15m if errors > 1%). Applying pattern-match override for txn_.* to prefer issue_refund.

ricardo: Will follow up with customer once canary confirms. Also adding repro curl + request_id to INC-4321 now. Thanks. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll run a quick test after the canary flips and report back.

jamie: Also adding a validation hotfix to gateway to reject apply_credit when args.invoice_id matches txn_.* (should never be an invoice). That will block this mismatch until we change signatures.

ricardo: Notes for postmortem: - ambiguous tool vocab - missing pre-exec schema validation - model routing heuristic too sensitive to token overlap

support-bot: INC-4321 updated: assigned to eng-tooling, priority P1 (customer-facing billing).

ash: I'll draft the longer-term API change doc (signature/intent enum) and post to #eng-ml and #eng-platform in the morning.

ricardo: Thanks everyone, keeping customer updated.
